title: Tenant-bound region smoothing and variant funnel
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Tenants are seeing noisy region switching and unexpectedly high cost when traffic spikes force 'immediate spill' to hosted resources. We need a routing policy that smooths region affinity for tenant sessions, provides predictable tier routing (dedicated first, then cost-effective fallbacks), and funnels model variant choices safely when capacity or latency SLOs are at risk.

Goal: Implement a per-tenant region-affinity smoothing layer plus a configurable variant funnel that: (1) reduces oscillation between regions during transient load, (2) enforces tier-aware backpressure (dedicated -> reserved shared -> hosted) with cost and latency weighting, and (3) exposes intuitive knobs for customers and operators to tune risk/cost trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New policy is wired into routing decision path and can be toggled per-tenant via config.
2) EWMA-based region affinity prevents >80% of region flips observed in baseline chaos tests.
3) Variant funnel enforces dedicated-first semantics with at most one automatic demotion to hosted per request under overload.
4) No regression in p95 latency for P0 tenants (>99% of load) in canary.
5) Dashboard surfaces region affinity score, demotions, and cost delta per tenant.
6) Runbook includes clear steps for manual rollback and throttling adjustments.
notes:
Design notes and decisions:
- Chosen smoothing algorithm: EWMA on successful request ratio + latency penalty to compute a region affinity score per tenant-region. Smoothing alpha default 0.25; configurable per-tenant. Rationale: simple, low-memory, incremental updates suited to streaming requests.
- Variant funnel ordering: dedicated_variant -> quantized_dedicated_variant -> regional_shared_variant -> hosted_variant. Only one auto-demotion allowed per request to avoid cascading quality loss.
- Backpressure model: token-bucket per-tenant per-region representing 'dedicated capacity credits'. When credits depleted, policy consults 'cost_weight' and 'latency_slack' to choose the next variant.
- Fairness: We implement soft reservations for P0 tenants (priority decay over time) to avoid long-term starvation for lower-priority customers while preserving contractual guarantees.
- Cost weighting: operators can set a multiplier (0.0 - 2.0) that biases routing toward cheaper hosted variants during high-cost events. Default 1.0.
- Safety heuristics: circuit-breaker if region p99 latency > 2x SLO or error rate > 1% sustained over 30s. In that case we trigger regional evacuation with staggered demote and an emergency backfill to hosted only for critical tenants.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (spike): implement region-affinity service and expose APIs for reads/writes (in-memory, Redis fallback). Add unit tests for EWMA and affinity decay. (ENG-15822-spike branch).
- Phase 2 (engine): integrate variant funnel into router with token-bucket enforcement and cost weighting knobs. Add feature flag per-tenant. Load test harness with synthetic tenants.
- Phase 3 (canary): 1% of traffic for 48h, monitor metrics; 10% for 24h; full rollout.

Metrics to track (added to Console):
- region_affinity_score_{tenant,region} (0-1),
- region_flips_per_10min_{tenant},
- demotions_count_by_variant_{tenant},
- p50/p95/p99 latency by tier,
- cost_delta_vs_baseline_{tenant},
- emergency_backfill_events,
- token_bucket_utilization_{tenant,region}.

- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/2345

- Runbook snippet: https://docs.redwood.ai/ops/runbooks/region-evacuation (preliminary)

Open questions and trade-offs noted during design review:
- Tight smoothing reduces flips but can increase latency when legitimate region shifts (persistent failovers) happen; mitigation: expose a TTL override to force immediate region affinity reset for operators.
- Single-demotion rule simplifies rollback but may increase cost due to hosted usage; mitigation: allow tenant opt-in for deeper demotions in exchange for lower cost SLAs.

Implementation blockers:
- Need a consistent token for 'tenant priority tier' from billing service (dependence on PM-412).
- Redis provisioning for affinity store must be coordinated with infra (ticket INF-881).
qa_plan: Unit tests for EWMA and token-bucket; integration tests that simulate regional outages and validate single-demotion guarantee; synthetic tenants with mixed priorities for load tests; chaos test that kills region nodes and asserts no more than X region flips per tenant. Detailed scenarios and thresholds in the design doc.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated per-tenant. Stage 0: internal traffic only. Stage 1: 1% customer traffic (48h), monitor p95 and demotions. Stage 2: 10% (24h) with extended cost monitoring. Stage 3: gradual ramp to 100% with automated rollback guard if p95 regresses beyond 10% of baseline or emergency_backfill_events > 2 in 1h.
